Callous

/KAL-us/ — stress on KAL · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Someone who is callous shows no concern for other people's pain and acts without sympathy toward them.

Only a callous landlord would raise the rent the week after the fire.

Worked Example

The landlord was callous about the family's eviction, telling them to leave by Friday without discussing hardship or flexibility.

Callus (hardened, thickened skin) + -ous (like, full of) = like hardened skin, or full of callus. Just as thick, hardened skin doesn't feel pain or sensation, a callous person's heart doesn't feel or respond to others' pain. The morpheme tells the story: emotional hardness mirrors physical hardness.

How Callous Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

heartless

heartless: completely lacking pity or kindness

indifferent

indifferent: having no interest or concern at all

apathetic

apathetic: feeling no emotion or motivation whatsoever

Antonyms

sympathetic

sympathetic: sharing and caring about others' feelings

compassionate

compassionate: moved to help those who suffer

How Strong Is It? — detached → indifferent → cold → callous

detached vs. callous

detached vs. callous: A detached observer keeps a polite distance, but a callous one looks straight past real suffering.

indifferent vs. callous

indifferent vs. callous: An indifferent neighbor doesn't notice your trouble; a callous neighbor notices and doesn't care.

cold vs. callous

cold vs. callous: A cold reply merely lacks warmth, but a callous reply tramples on someone's feelings.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — call

Root — call: hardened skin (from Latin callus, 'hardened skin' — callus is still a real English word for a patch of toughened skin)

Suffix — -ous

Suffix — -ous: like, full of (Latin -osus)

Put it together

Put it together: Call ('hardened skin,' from Latin callus — callus is still a real English word for a patch of toughened skin) + -ous ('like, full of') — callous means 'like hardened skin': figuratively, a heart so toughened it no longer feels other people's pain.

Use the root in a new word: callus

Use the root in a new word: callus: Years of guitar practice left a callus on each of her fingertips.

Root Check

Word Choice

neutral

Reach for callous when someone shows a striking lack of concern or sympathy in a situation where compassion would be expected. A callous remark, a callous attitude, a callous decision—the word emphasizes emotional hardness, not just being tough or strict. It's more damning than indifference because it implies active indifference.
